newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: S.African stock market closing report.
newsitem.headline: S.African stock market closing report.

text.p: South African shares ended firmer after active trade, with industrials rising to a record closing high on institutional buying and gold shares down on bullion failing to stay above the $320 per ounce level.

"The market is looking good on industrials and slightly soft on golds with the bullion price trying throughout the day to go through $320," James Scott, equity marketing manager at Societe General Frankel Pollack told Reuters.
Dealers said the market was active, driven by local and offshore interest with some futures play and trade was not dominated by single trades, with overall volumes traded worth 900 million rand.
Financial stocks saw strong interest which pushed the financial index up 75.8 points to an all-time closing high of 10,321.9 points.
Dealers said an interest switch from technology stocks to financial stocks was being seen.
Liberty Life gained 450 cents to 146 rand and First National added 60 cents to 39.10 rand.
The industrial index surged 50.7 points to 8,936.4 points, the gold index fell 7.1 points to 969.2 points and the all-share index rose 32.1 points to 7,422.8 points.
In the broader market, advancing issues outpaced declining issues by 188 to 179 with 144 issues unchanged.
Edgars finished unchanged at 131 rand in a volume of 45 million shares.
IBM gained 118 cents to 976 cents amid perceptions the firm's planned restructuring could enchance future earnings growth, dealers said.
Durban Deep dropped 320 cents to 10.00 rand after parent company Randgold announced revised ratios for its merger with Buffelsfontein and Blyvooruitzicht.
Randgold was down 50 cents to 16 rand, Blyvoor shed 25 cents to 250 cents and Buffels clipped 30 cents to 980 rand.

Forbes rose to a new year high of 10.60 rand after the company said it had made a cash offer to increase its stake in British marine insurance firm Neslon Hurst Plc, dealers said. The share ended up 80 cents to 10.30 rand.

Near-dated gold share futures were firm in late trade after starting weaker as bullion rose above the $320 per ounce level, although it lost its grip later on. Industrials were boosted by a firmer Wall Street overnight and stronger bonds at the finish.
The market was seen firm on Thursday with golds tracking movement in the bullion price.
The September all-share contract stood at 6,745/58 from 6,719, the gold contract was at 696/700 from a 690 settlement and the industrial contract at 8,632/35 from 8,588.
